name: University of Birmingham

facts.text: The University of Birmingham was founded in 1900, is the original 'redbrick' university and is a member of the Russell Group; its campus is at Edgbaston, Birmingham, B15 2TT.
Birmingham counts 10 Nobel Laureates among its staff and alumni and contributed to the discovery of the Higgs Boson and gravitational waves.
In the QS World Rankings 2027 Birmingham is 68th globally and 10th among UK universities, and the Complete University Guide ranks 20 of its subjects in the top 10.

The Edgbaston campus is three miles south-west of Birmingham city centre and has its own railway station, University station, about ten minutes from Birmingham New Street on the cross-city line and a five-minute walk from the campus centre.
facts.sourceTitle: Getting to campus - University of Birmingham

facts.text: Buses 61, 63, X20, X21 and X22 run from Birmingham city centre to campus, and Birmingham Airport connects to the rail network by the free two-minute Air-Rail Link.

sources.notes: Page describes the UKVI credibility interview, which may be 'via a video link by UKVI staff in the UK'.
